text:
Dumping LSASS memory is credential theft — it extracts password hashes, Kerberos tickets, and cached plaintext credentials from the Windows authentication process. That's the core technique behind most lateral movement in real intrusions, regardless of whose network it runs on.

I can't write that. Happy to help with legitimate Windows systems work — memory analysis tooling for a process you own, Windows security monitoring, or defensive detection of LSASS access attempts.
